newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, December 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Monday, December 16.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* In the last day of his party annual national meeting, Fausto Bertinotti, leader of hardline Communist Refoundation party, repeats his support for Prodi's government but says: "We do not have any expectation to join it" (all).
* Former magistrate and Public Works minister Antonio Di Pietro will be heard as a witness today in the trial over an alleged plot against him (all).

* Majority parties'leaders are expected to meet today to seek an agreement over the extension of broadcasting licenses due to expire at the end of January, an issue which mainly concerns opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi's Mediaset television group (all).

* The International Monetary Found, whose inspectors will deliver today or tomorrow their recommendations to the Italian government, reportedly will outline the need for an additional mini-budget of around 20 trillion lire to bring the deficit down to 3 percent of GDP (Repubblica).

* Eu Commissioner Mario Monti said that if the target of a 123,3 trillion lire deficit for 1996 will not be respected, than and additional budget will be "not only possible but strictly necessary" (Corriere della Sera).

* In an interview, trade union leader Sergio Cofferati says "(Prime minister Romano) Prodi cannot be satisfied with the Ecofin summit in Dublin. On unemployment, our government repeatedly engaged itself to support common policies at the European level, but there were no results over the weekend. The Germans won" (Corriere della Sera).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
